page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.large is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS Graviton processors. It features an arm64 architecture utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 model with 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and includes a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance store. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-threaded performance in specific workloads, with gzip compression reaching 36.33 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.2 GB/sec, both placing in the top tier. However, multi-core and multi-threaded capabilities are more limited, as shown by a weak stress-ng multi-core score of 4005.17 and a poor PassMark CPU score of 2191.41. Memory performance is mixed; while the PassMark memory score is strong at 2876.9, memory write bandwidth for large blocks is weak at 25.15 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform at an average level, achieving 6.51 million operations per second for Redis.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m9gd.large offers a balanced resource profile for entry-level workloads requiring local NVMe storage without the overhead of larger instances. The primary tradeoff is the low vCPU count and weak multi-threaded scaling, making it less suitable for parallel processing or heavy multi-threaded applications. It is best suited for single-threaded tasks, lightweight database operations, static web serving, and basic caching layers.
